items.title: Kepler College Student Showcase 2026
items.summary:
Join us in celebrating our proud, soon-to-be graduates of the Kepler College Diploma Program as they present in fulfillment of their final Demonstration of Learning.

As the capstone of their scholastic achievement, these presentations showcase the depth and breadth of their astrological studies, inviting us to witness the knowledge, insight, and dedication they have cultivated throughout their journey.

· Jennifer Lewis, "Are You Likely to Move?"

This project seeks to answer the question of "are you likely to move" which supplements the Astro*Carto*Graphy* question of "where should I move". This analysis argues that the elemental and modal placements of planets and lunar nodes offer predictive insight into an individual's predisposition toward relocation.


· Elizabeth Gossell, "The Astrology of Cyber Warfare"

Cyber warfare actions are a modern occurrence, but this research posits that astrological techniques can be used to predict the likelihood of a cyber warefare occurrence by empirically assessing known events and using astrological patterns to predict their occurrence with a reasonable degree of certainty.

· Wendy van Lierop-Lucassen, "Pluto Signs Describe Seven Distinct Generations"

When Pluto transits through the zodiac signs, the modalities of the signs (cardinal, fixed and mutable) describe how the signs express their energy as experienced by every generation.

· Jazzy Smith, "The Astrology of Bass"

A delineation of the charts of 40 well known bass vocalists and instrumentalists over many years to see if there is a common astrological theme that they share.

Hosted by Donna Young

To learn more about the Kepler College Professional Diploma in Astrology (KPDA) visit: https://www.keplercollege.org/diplomas/the-kepler-professional-diploma-in-astrology-kpda/

To view our current class offerings, visit: https://store.keplercollege.org/current-course-offerings/

How much astrology do you know?! Take our FREE quiz and find out here: https://store.keplercollege.org/product/free-kepler-college-placement-quiz/

items.title: Gnosticism, Hermeticism, and Ancient Astrology
items.summary:
Scholar M. David Litwa joins the podcast to explore the intersections of Gnosticism, Hermeticism, and ancient astrology.

David is a historian of early Christianity and Greco-Roman religions who recently published a new translation of the Corpus Hermeticum. Together, we trace how these esoteric traditions developed and interacted in the ancient world, particularly in the cultural melting pot of Alexandria.

We discuss the emergence of Hermeticism as a synthesis of Egyptian religion and Greek philosophy, and how early Christian Gnosticism subsequently adapted many of these cosmological frameworks. A major focal point is how ancient astrology, including the ascent and descent of the soul through the planetary spheres, was integrated into these religious movements. We contrast the Gnostic view of the planets as restrictive archons keeping the soul imprisoned with the more sympathetic Hermetic view of the visible cosmos as a second God and part of divine providence.

We also take a close look at the Peratics, a unique Gnostic group that integrated technical Hellenistic astrology directly into their religion in order to map the soul’s escape from the material realm. Finally, we unpack the historical tensions between fate, providence, and free will, examining how early Christians navigated astrological determinism before figures like Augustine firmly pushed back against the practice. This conversation highlights the profound impact that Hellenistic astrology had on the broader philosophical and religious landscape of the ancient world. 

This is episode 546 of The Astrology Podcast.
